Among OSA models, PGS005220 shows the strongest overall visible evidence package: disease-focused publication context, very high reported full-model AUROC (0.79), a strong effect size (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.39–1.68), multi-ancestry evaluation support listed, and reasonable validation size (n=21,975). It is preferred over ExPRSweb sleep-apnea scores whose reported AUROCs are ~0.49–0.527 (near chance) and come from a pan-trait repository context. Main limitation: PGS005220 includes BMI in covariates (risk-factor/mediator adjustment) and reports only full-model AUROC (no PGS-only/incremental metrics), reducing comparability and preventing a high-confidence selection; additionally PGS003857/PGS003858 report AUROC=0.77 but are sparse (6–18 SNPs) and similarly BMI-adjusted, and PGS005219 has comparable AUROC with a larger OR but adjusted-BMI framing, leaving some unresolved competition within the OSA family.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer), with endpoint fidelity supported by phenotyping fields such as “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Testicular cancer/incident testicular cancer.” Among the Cancer PRSweb cluster, PGS000604 is the strongest supported choice in the visible evidence: it has the highest reported AUROC within that coherent family (full_model AUROC 0.703, 95% CI 0.659–0.745) and the highest Nagelkerke’s pseudo-R² (0.0882) with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and consistent European ancestry evaluation, and it is trained/validated in UKB with larger training/validation than the MGI-based siblings (training n=1,671; validation n=1,484). Confidence is Moderate because key metrics are largely full-model (not clearly PRS-only) across candidates, and cross-study comparability remains limited despite the within-family advantage for PGS000604.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (testicular carcinoma) with endpoint-faithful phenotypes such as “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Testicular cancer,” predominantly evaluated in European ancestry. All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (thyroid carcinoma / thyroid cancer) by trait_efo and generally by phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match model is available. All 20 candidates are direct matches on disease concept (bladder cancer / urinary bladder carcinoma) with generally similar endpoint phrasing (mostly “Cancer of bladder” or “Incident bladder cancer”). Many models report only full-model AUROC (often with age/sex/smoking/BMI covariates), which domain guidance flags as not PRS-comparable; notably the very high AUROC ~0.80 for PGS000071/PGS000782 is likely dominated by covariates (age/smoking/BMI) and cannot be treated as strong PRS evidence without PGS-only or incremental metrics. Among models with more PRS-informative signals, the PRSweb ‘GWAS Hits’ scores show the best combination of endpoint alignment and effect-size/metrics in the provided metadata; PGS000611 (UKB-trained, 13 variants) has full-model AUROC 0.567 with additional supportive risk-stratification evidence (top 1% vs rest OR 2.66 [1.79–3.93] and per-SD OR 1.284 [1.211–1.361]) and a larger validation sample (n=13,530) than other PRSweb bladder candidates. Limitation: the evidence base remains imperfect because PRS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental AUROC are not provided for most candidates (including PGS000611), and several near-tied PRSweb siblings (e.g., PGS000610/PGS000612/PGS000613) have very similar AUROC/effect sizes, so the preference is not decisive.

All 20 candidates are direct matches to urinary bladder cancer/bladder cancer (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are aligned, mostly EUR evaluation). Among them, PGS000071 has strong endpoint fidelity (incident bladder cancer), very large validation support (n=391,888), and reports time-to-event effect size evidence (HR=1.28, 95% CI 1.20–1.37) plus C-index 0.813. However, its reported AUROC (0.803) is a full-model metric with multiple non-genetic covariates (age/sex/PCs plus smoking variables and BMI), and PRS-only/incremental discrimination is not provided, so the apparent high AUROC may be largely covariate-driven. Competing PRSweb scores (e.g., PGS000611/PGS000613) provide more PRS-focused metrics (AUROC ~0.57; OR top 1% vs rest up to 2.91) but are smaller validations and still not clearly PRS-only; portability-family scores (PGS001807/PGS002017) report only weak partial correlations (~0.018–0.020) without AUC. Given the evidence mix and lack of clean PRS-only metrics across the set, PGS000071 is the best-supported direct-match choice but with only moderate confidence.
